newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich - Clinton must find votes for fast-track.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich - Clinton must find votes for fast-track.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Tuesday the House would move fast-track trade authority as soon as President Clinton found some Democratic votes to support it.

"We'd move fast-track the minute the administration can help us find some Democratic votes and can agree on language," Gingrich told reporters after testifying at a hearing. He said the president needed to bring 90 votes for the legislation.
"The President needs to bring about 90 votes with him," Gingrich said. "I think we could almost certainly carry fast-track if he gave us the 90 votes."

Fast-track would give the president authority to negotiate a trade agreement without fear that Congress would amend it, because Congress would have to vote either for or against the proposed agreement without amendment.
Asked if he thought there would be a budget deal this week, Gingrich replied, "I certainly hope so." He declined to comment further on budget questions.
